NC: 2023:KHC:32898 3.

Learned Senior counsel for the petitioner drawing attention of this court to the provisions of Section 38D of the Act submits that when the Act itself provides for regularisation of unauthorised occupation, the impugned order passed by the Government at Annexure-Q is unsustainable.

Further drawing attention of this Court to the resolution of the BDA dated 15.02.2011 produced at Annexure-F, page 85 and resolution No.32/2017 dated 18.04.2017 which is part of Annexure-K at page No.110, learned Senior counsel submits that BDA has in fact resolved the issue of regularisation in favour of the petitioner.
Thus, he submits that in view of the aforesaid legal and factual position of the matter, the issuance of the order by the Government at Annexure-Q cannot be sustained.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- BDA submits that acquisition and construction of buildings by the petitioner have taken place admittedly subsequent to issuance of preliminary notification and the final NC: 2023:KHC:32898 notification respectively.
He therefore submits that acquisition having attained finality the petitioner would not be entitled to seek a regularisation.
Therefore, he submits that there is no infirmity in the order impugned.
5. Heard.
Perused the records.

6. There is no dispute of the fact that Preliminary notification was issued in the year 1978 and the Final notification was issued in the year 1985 and there is also no dispute of the fact that petitioner herein acquired the subject property in the year 1984 and has put up structures/buildings subsequently thereafter.

(3) The Bangalore Development Authority shall take up an action plan to evict the unauthorized occupants in Bangalore Development Authority Lands and who are not eligible for allotment of site under this section on the date of commencement of the Bangalore Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2020, within two years from the date of commencement of the Amendment Act."

Perusal of the same makes it clear that there is a provision enabling the BDA to allot the land in favour of the original owner or purchaser or unauthorised occupant NC: 2023:KHC:32898 as the case may be if found to be in possession twelve years prior to the date of insertion of Section 38D of the Act i.e., with effect from 10.07.2020.
Admittedly, in the instant case, the petitioner having purchased the property in the year 1984 has apparently has put up construction thereafter.

Now that there is an enabling provisions providing for allotment as noted above, the impugned order passed by the Government on 12.12.2019 prior to the amendment to the Act, solely on the premise that there is no provision under the law either to exclude the land from acquisition or to regularize the occupation will not survive.

10. At this juncture, learned counsel for the respondent-BDA submits that to avail the benefit of Section 38D of the Act, the parties seeking benefit thereunder shall admit their land having been vested with the authority.
It is only thereafter, consideration of regularization would arise.
He also submits that writ petition in W.P.No.14959/2020 (PIL) is pending consideration challenging the very provisions of Section 38D of the Act and Rules framed thereunder.

He also submits that in the said Public Interest Litigation a conditional interim order has been passed to the effect that if in the event of BDA granting relief under Section 38D of the Act, the grantee should be put on notice that such regularisation would be subject to the out come of the W.P.No.14959/2020 (PIL) which is pending consideration.
Be that as it is.

In view of the aforesaid factual position this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent-BDA to consider the case of the petitioner in the light of provisions of Section 38D of the Act and in the light of the interim order passed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.14959/2020 (PIL) within an outer limit of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

12. It is made clear that petitioner is also at liberty to make necessary representation seeking compensation including interest to the respondent-BDA and upon such representation the same shall be considered by the respondent-BDA in accordance with law.
